newsitem.title: UK: British MPs reject return to caning in schools.
newsitem.headline: British MPs reject return to caning in schools.

text.p: Right-wing members of Britain's ruling Conservative Party, opposed both by the government and opposition parties, failed on Tuesday in an attempt to bring caning back to British schools.
An amendment to the government's education bill that would have allowed state schools to reintroduce corporal punishment was defeated in the lower House of Commons by 376 votes to 101.
Prime Minister John Major gave rank-and-file Conservatives permission to vote according to their consciences but ordered ministers to toe the government line and oppose the amendment.
If the measure had passed, Britain would have come into conflict with the European Court of Human Rights, which has outlawed corporal punishment.

The measure was sponsored by Conservative MP James Pawsey, chairman of parliament's education committee, who said caning was a reasonable punishment that would improve discipline and standards in schools.
"Some of our schools have been reduced to savage anarchy and there is no discipline and without discipline there can be no education," another Conservative, Tony Marlow, said during the debate.
But opposition MPs said there was no evidence to show that caning improved discipline in schools.
Peter Kilfoyle, an education spokesman for the opposition Labour Party, attacked Pawsey's measure as "neanderthal".
"I can think of nothing more barbaric than state-sanctioned assault on children and that is what is being advocated tonight," Kilfolyle said.
